title: Improved by Mixing it with Water & Olive Oil
text: I was a little concerned when after already purchasing three bottles all at once I read the reviews about the scent being too strong “baby powder” and the moisturizing aspect not effective to help create soft hair. But I modified the product before use which helped tremendously with the scent and hopefully with the moisturizing as well. I combined 1/3 water, 1/3 olive oil and 1/3 of the leave in conditioner in a spray bottle to use as a moisturizer in my daughter’s hair. It drastically cut the scent down to a minimum... it is a faint and manageable scent now with more notes of almond milk and less perfumery smell. This product does contain alcohol in the ingredients which I’m guessing is why others have experienced dryness from use. My daughter has 4c black hair, damaged from straightening/relaxers and we’re trying to return back to a natural style so I thought it reasonable to give this product a try. We go through leave-ins like water so the water/olive oil mixture should do well to extend the use and supplement. Too soon to tell final results which is partially why I’m rating this an average three stars (also because of the strong scent) but so far so good. I would recommend only if you are not afraid to experiment.

title: This is fun and also challenging!
text:
There is a pretty big learning curve when using this for the first time. Some things I did that made it easier:

1. You need Vaseline to help mold when it’s on your skin. It says this in the instructions but I had to buy some.
2. If you are doing something like a scar similar to the look I did, I found it easier to mold the wax and adhere it first. Then, use setting powder to hold it in place. Lastly, you can use the pointed end of the tool that is provided to “slice” and make it look real. If you slice first and then use the setting powder, it doesn’t work as well.
3. Getting this off your face with the spirit gum is challenging. I used a combination of nuetrogena makeup wipes, Vaseline, and a face scrub to do that job.
4. Watch videos. I found this to be the most helpful before starting. There are so many tutorials out there.

I hope this helps.

title: Fresh as a daisy
text:
I normally get the normal Salux from my local Asian grocery, pharmacy, or beauty store. I often get compliments on my soft skin, which I attribute to using this to exfoliate and moisturizing immediately after a shower, but before toweling off. The Salux design works really well to get hard to reach spots like your back and the bottoms of your feet. I've tried off brand towel washcloths and loofah fibers were way too soft. It was time to replace my regular Salux, but after recently moving, it wasn't a priority to get a new one, and was without for a couple weeks.

I don't really get body acne, but I felt crusty and clogged for going a couple of weeks without exfoliating! I could feel hair conditioner on my back not fully rinsed away, even though I showered every day.After getting settled in to my new place, I had finally had it and placed an order for this "hard"(lol) version. The tasteful grey color actually matched the color scheme of my new bathroom. The first shower that I took once I received this was so refreshing! I felt like a snake shedding its skin, like a Phoenix reborn in cleansing fire. It was the satisfaction of scratching an itch except the itch is on your entire body. I love the feeling of a brand new Salux! Hopefully the "hard" version sustains that feeling for longer. It's holy grail right now, until I can find something that's as effective but zero waste. On that note, a Salux is more hygienic and sustainable than a regular loofah because the knotted fibers of a loofah don't dry completely and are therefore more susceptible to bacteria and mildeww growth.

title: Non-irritating & Soothing cleanser
text:
This has brought relief. My eyelids and lashes get a thorough cleansing with no irritation or burning whatsoever.

I had cataract surgery 6 months ago and was prescribed steroid drops for 2 weeks after the procedure. Initially, I had minimal issues with irritation, dry feeling or redness. Same experience after the procedure was completed on the 2nd eye.

Approximately a month after the 2nd procedure, both eyes, but especially the right one, were no longer white (slight redness), were irritated and felt dry and scratchy. I began using the Systane eye drops that I had been given at the time of surgery but, in short order, I made an appointment with the ophthalmologist. He put me back on a reduced frequency of the steroid drops for a short time period and during the follow up(s) recommended that I continue using Systane to relieve the dry, itchy, irritating sensation.

I “did“ the Systane for a month or so but noticed my eyelids were slightly more “crusty” in the morning than I had ever experienced. Then a major redness (in both eyes) hit. It was so bad that I thought that I had pink eye.

Back to the ophthalmologist, (No, I haven’t changed shampoo or laundry detergent; Yes, I still work in a clean room, environmentally controlled lab; No, I don’t have any new workplace exposures) back on the steroid drops and still needing Systane (several times/day) to temporarily relieve the dry scratchy feeling.

Little did I know that statistically over 30% of all cataract surgery patients experience the same irritation and dryness issues that I did. Most, like my mother-in-law, simply rely on eye drops for relief - in my mother-in-laws case - 4 times per day for over 2 years since her surgery.

The relief for me has been a combination of incorporating the Bruder eye heat pad (w/hygienic eyelid sheets) and the OCuSOFT Oust Demodex cleanser. The improvement in my eye discomfort level was almost immediate. In the 2 weeks that I have used this combo I have used ZERO eye drops.

I specifically chose the OCuSOFT Oust Demodex cleanser because an ophthalmologist stated in his review that it was “tolerated” by virtually all of his patients for daily use.

Did I have Demodex mites or clogged eyelid oil glands or just getting old? I don’t know, but the Bruder heat combined with the the OCuSOFT Oust Demodex cleanser (Tulip Oil) worked for me without any discomfort. Totally Satisfied!

title: It’s helping!
text:
I have mild rosacea that has been flaring up for the past two months. At the same time my eyes had become itchy and I was waking up with a little bit of crusty stuff in the corners. While watching Dr. Pimple Popper I saw her treat someone with rosacea. When she explained that rosacea sufferers have an excess of microscopic mites I knew I had to investigate treatment for myself. I quickly googled it and found that using an eye wash like this can help kill the mites. I bought this and a tea tree face wash in Saturday and they were delivered Sunday. I immediately broke open the package and went to wash my eyes and face. I used this in my eyes first and they felt better immediately. My case wasn’t super severe, so I’m sure that helped. Still, I am happy with the progress that using this for 4 days has given me. Eyes haven’t felt itchy, no junk in corners, nor red and irritated. I used one pump of foam, rub it on my eyes concentrating on my lashes, then rinse with warm water. Based on how little product takes to wash, I will have this bottle for quite a while.

I really feel like it has helped! Give it a try!

title: Lots of settings & great air flow
text:
I really love this blow dryer. My prior dryer, a compact model with 1875 watts, gave up when I caught my now-long hair in the fan. When I set out to replace it, I wanted a dryer that would be easy to clean out if I should do this again.

This dryer has a removable cover on the fan that makes it simple to clean. It is 1875 watts, with three heat levels, three wind speeds, and a cool shot feature. It comes with several attachments for straightening hair, for drying curly hair, and for concentrating air flow. I've tested them all out by now, and each is effective.

This is not a compact dryer, but more of a mid-size. That said it is not particularly heavy. It has a lot of features without a very large price. It is small enough that it's easy to pack, but it's very powerful and moves a lot of air. I find it dries my hair faster than my prior hair dryers, and I don't have a lot of frizzy, fly-away hair after using it.

I bought this as a lightning deal so it was discounted from the full price, but I feel like it's a great dryer at any price. I recommend it.

title: Some brushes are better than others.
text: I got these brushes when they were on sale ($9 for 32 brushes...), and I didn't expect much for the price but I read some reviews and they seemed worth your money.  They came in an easily-washable bag and were organized by size, none were missing, and they were packaged well.  I didn't notice a bad chemical smell like some reviews said they had, but I still washed them like you should with any new brush.  The larger brushes, like the contour, blush, etc.  brushes were quite soft and flexible, the bristles flex and conform to your face.  But the small brushes were just very dense and hard to use.  They were very stiff and rigid.  They felt soft in your fingers but when you use them on your face, they don't flex much and they get kind of pokey.  The only use for the small eye brushes is packing, because you cant use them like a regular brush because of their stiffness.  They were just too dense, that's all.  But the larger brushes are very soft and good for blending.  They apply product evenly and smoothly.  I use them quite often.  They tend to not pick up much product, at least for me, so you have to keep dipping them into the pans often.  But I would say that the larger brushes are worth your money.
